translation:
The lung is the master of water. When heat overflows it then dissolves; when it dissolves then the source of water is exhausted. Earth is the mother of metal; if it does not receive [the lung], then metal has no generation. The three viscera of earth, metal and water daily waste away. If there is no jade fluid, how can the divine essence return? Though I plan a forbidden formula, it is but relying on the common talk of the ancients for this already weary formed body.
When heart yin is vacuous then one easily sweats; when lung yin is vacuous then cough is much; when liver yin is vacuous then fire rises; when kidney yin is vacuous then fever develops; when spleen yin is vacuous then the stools are loose. Is this not a single true yin? It is the beginning of a timid (consumptive) pattern. One only knows that treating a headache as headache is the mark of the good physician; one does not know that when you tread on frost, solid ice approaches, and that the gentleman should hold a mind of worry and caution.
The pulse on examination is thin, rapid and faint; the tongue is dry and yellow; there is diarrhea; the body is parched and withered and not moist. This is injury to yin from excessive diarrhea, and by this the heat pathogen has sunk inward, which is greatly to be concerned about. The method of treatment is to be light in clearing the pathogen and bitter in draining its heat. Whether this should be so, I do not know.
One who is not harmonious in food and drink has depleted the taiyin. Ge Zhichuan's Handbook of Prescriptions for Emergencies (肘後方) has a single-ingredient method for treating vacuity strain. If shaoyin and jueyin are depleted, use the Lujiao powder; if taiyin is depleted, use the Shenqu powder. Now I use the Shenqu powder.
The middle burner is the place where qi, blood and fluids assemble. Now the gastric qi is unable to spread and course within the vessels; this is also a depletion of the original qi within. Use sourness to restrain and gather the leaking; use pungency to flow and move; only use sweetness to cultivate and nurture. Because a swelling affliction increased, I have set this [method] aside. I plan a formula to serve for your perusal.
There are fourteen reversals. Draining is one method, and settling is one method. When the crooked and straight (wood) exceeds, not only does it insult earth, but it also above does not fear metal. The settling method, I fear, will not be compatible due to this conflict; following its trend to guide it beneficially, and only then moistening and nourishing it—there are few in whom this does not succeed.
The book of Zhongjing says: 'The malaria pulse is naturally stringlike.' A single phrase opens up the vision of people and heaven. Now within the three sections and nine indicators, not a trace of stringlike sign can be seen. What contends with the upright qi is not comparable to the spring wind, the summer heat, or the miasma of the south. Reasoning from this, more than half is understood.
The more the pulse is pressed the larger it becomes, so one may know that the yin qi is insufficient, allowing the malaria pathogen to penetrate deeply. Lu lou (Radix Gentianae longdancao) and biejia are over-supplementing yin, and are not fitting for a sixty-year-old body that toils the heart. When the sweat is vented too much, one must also be concerned for the yang qi. Between the stomach there is hidden pathogen, and water and drink do not enter—all these the body cannot bear. How could it be drained from the seat of sweat again? Let the patient be careful and the physician prudent.
It is clearly liver wind mounting upward; the left foot pulse is fragmented, chaotic and pounding the finger. This is the same origin of yi and gui; kidney and liver are jointly diseased. But the shaoyin pulse does not reach the crown of the head; only yin can reach. Take the liver as most severe and the kidney next.
This is because metal and water do not mutually receive and hold up each other, hence the cough lasts long without healing. Never regulate the lung; the lung is a delicate viscus, the more one regulates it the more vacuous it becomes. The pattern also must not be recklessly and generally nourished in yin.
Shortness of breath and loss of voice, with a water-chicken sound now and again in the throat; the right pulse is like leather; the face is swollen and the color withered; the lung and stomach respond to this; below the heart there is glomus and hardness. Supplementation and draining have been altered in confusion, yet moving [them] has not yielded a single effect. It is severe in the water season and violent in the midst of spring. I plan to present the combined tang of the wei-jing and yuebi (Waste-leaf and Great-Boiling Decoctions); take three doses in drink.
This originally belongs to damp-warmth, transforming within the triple burner and filling the interstices. Mistakenly wounding the qi of hand taiyin and foot taiyang will necessarily gradually enter the path of vacuity depletion. This is not the fault of the illness, it is the fault of the treatment. One must move to an eminent, bright and quiet void chamber and treat over a hundred days; then perhaps one may obtain it. I plan a formula to open the taiyang and benefit the taiyin.
A stringlike-moved and heartless pulse is called stomach-stinginess (胃少). Though it is not the 'only stringlike without stomach' of the Classic of Difficult Issues, for a chronic illness to have this is not well. Do not, because of loss of blood, long administer pure-yin medicinals. The yang qi is suppressed and the yin has nothing to rely on. In my humble view, at the moment advance sweet-warm. Jianzhong tang adding renshen, zhi mianqi (honey-roasted astragalus), and guishen.
The disease lies in the extraordinary channels; treating the other channels does not respond. Once one knows that the blood travels the clear path, one knows that the clear qi is not purifying, hence the nose turns red and there is fainting. Both emerge from the governing vessel. Delighting in the unusual is of no use. Treating with the ancient method, one naturally gets results.
Summer heat is the yin pathogen within heat. The heart first receives it; it enters the uterus of the covering (pericardium channel). Languid and mute, with spirit-clouding and cold limbs, is incurable. Now the pulse is slow and soft, gradually there is this tendency, and the four extremities gradually become cold; indeed there is the fear of internal closure and external desertion. Urgently use the method of freeing yang and rescuing reversal, following the meaning of the right great shun powder. I know not how this fares.
The right pulse is hollow and bounding; the ears are deaf; blood overflows downward; chills and fever do not stop. Because the yin collaterals are wounded, and the jueyin does not restrain, one should vent the heat pathogen forth from the extreme yin—this is the first principle of preserving yin.
Right pulse one breath seven beats, stringlike; right pulse one breath six beats, tense (the original text has 'right pulse' twice, from the Zhejiang Journal of Chinese Medicine); coughing so that one cannot catch the breath. The yin qi is already weak, and metal and water are jointly diseased. Moreover I discuss the Jingyue Six-Monarchs decoction for the metal and water and administer it.
Naturally there is a wheezing pattern; the form and qi are timid and weak; the throat is painful but not swollen; one coughs from time to time. This is newly contracted wind-warmth in the lung, and the qi does not purify and descend. One should still clear and downbear.
The endowment is already thin and the cough with red sputum very easily wounds yin. One must not regulate the lung, because water issues from the high plateau (the lung). The lung governs the mother of qi, relying on it to engender fluids and supplement liquids, and to circulate through the hundred vessels.
This is the formula discussed together yesterday. Pressing the two gate positions, the pulse is stringlike. I particularly borrow the xuanfu-daizhe (Inula and hematite) method of Zhongjing and administer it together with the four-grind drink. Xuanhua (Inula) has a function of revolving and turning; daizhe is a settling and dropping product; salty and cold can descend, sour can enter the liver. The four-grind then gradually grinds and mobilizes, causing hand taiyin to carry out the order of clearing and purifying, and foot jueyin to have no violence of overcoming or insulting. Now the stringlike sign of the two gates has already diminished and the facial swelling has slightly retreated; the medicinals have already responded. Yet the sudden thirst with desire to drink continues as before. This is because in the yangming bowel the accumulated filth has not been dispelled; it scorches and boils the fluids; when below one day does not communicate, above one day rises and floats. Though there is a strategy to supplement the vacuity, who dares to administer it broadly? And the vacuous vessels and vacuous signs are clearly manifest, and the situation will not brook delay. Previously I borrowed the method of Zhongjing to retreat the string of the two gates; should I not alone be able to borrow Zhongjing's urgent removal of the old filth to preserve the fluids? Yet one cannot yet administer the hegemonic method of Zihe [Zhang Congzheng]. I plan a gentle method, pushing out the old and bringing the new. I still await the seal-approval of the two senior gentlemen of yesterday to see how it fares. [Medicinals] xuanfuhua, daizheshi, renshen, decocted and sent down with chenxiang huqi wan (Agarwood Transforming Qi Pill) two qian and five fen.
Ziyang yingye gao (Nourishing the Constructive and Moistening Liquid Paste):
nvzhenzi, guangpi, dry sangye, shudi, zaoliangcao (Ecliptae herba), baishao, heizhima (black sesame), gouqizi, fresh juhua, guishen, hei lüdou (black wild bean), yuzhu (Polygonati odorati rhizoma), nanzhu leaf, white fushen, shajili (Sablenae fructus), zhi gancao.
Right: the aforesaid first fourteen medicinals, four liang each; the last two medicinals two liang each. Simmer into an ointment over sacred spring water and mulberry-branch fire; incorporate genuine ejiao three liang and refined pure white honey three liang; store well in a porcelain jar. Daily at the mao hour take out five or six qian to take, sent down with boiled water.
This formula is the great medicinal for taking as food in retirement, and a fine product for liver qi disharmony. The two medicinals zhen (nvzhenzi) and lian (zaoliangcao) model the two solstices to secretly turn yin and yang. With the assistance of sang and ma (mulberry and hemp), it regulates the wind-qi in accord with the season and plants and sows life force. Aided by gou and ju (lycium and chrysanthemum), they form the rise and fall of spring and autumn, also conveying and transforming while bearing the flow. Gui and shao being pungent-sour, one opens and one drains, so that there is no stagnating or lingering emotion. Dihuang and jili, one filling and one nurturing, so that the muscles do not come to the distress of vacuity. Lüdou nourishes water and rests the liver; nanzhu builds the origin and augments qi. Fushen and yuzhu are the messengers of the constructive and defensive; juhong and gancao are the true officials of the throat and tongue. Ejiao, created from the Ji River, is the biting cold of stirring the turbid and lifting the clear; honey, brewed from a single flower, is the benevolence of gentle wind and sweet rain. Taking it not only orders the origin and dispels old age, but moreover shows that the generative life of heaven and earth is thus.
Xinpi shuangbu wan (Heart-Spleen Twofold Supplementation Pill):
renshen, yuanshen, wuweizi, yuanzhi (membrane), maidong, fushen, suanzaoren, baiziren, yuzhu (Atractylodes), chuanbei, sheng gancao, ku jiegeng (bitter platycodon), danshen, shengdi, chuan huanglian, Jinhua xiangfu, zhusha.
Right: make into powder; simmer guiyuan rou into a paste to substitute for honey, and pound into pills the size of a play-ball (彈子). Each morning chew one pill and send it down with boiled water.
The Canon says: 'The woman takes the heart and spleen as the root of establishing life.' For whenever heart-spleen qi is depressed, and depression follows fire, if it does not resolve for a long time it gradually consumes the five yin. I have especially made this formula, which has both freeing and supplementing, and is truly able to contend with masters like Danxi and Lizhai. The meaning of the formula is about: renshen nourishes the heart qi, maidong augments the heart fluids, shengdi and danshen augment the heart yin, fushen and yuanzhi settle the heart spirit, wuwei and zaoren gather the heart liquid, chuanlian and gancao drain the heart yang, jiegeng benefits the heart qi, zhusha settles the heart timidity, baizhu builds the spleen yang, xiangfu makes the spleen yin free-flowing, and chuanbei treats spleen depression. I especially weight their number to respond to the two viscera of heart and spleen; longan substitutes for honey to greatly supplement the heart blood, and gancao harmonizes the spleen. Make the pills the size of a play-ball and chew finely to swallow, so that they do not go straight down to the lower burner, and their effect is redoubled. It is named the heart-spleen twofold supplementation method.
Treating postpartum lower-abdominal binding masses (瘕):
renshen, yunmu (mica) powder, danggui, jinlingzi (Toosendan fructus), shengdi, wuzhuyu, stir-fried chishao, stir-fried bai chuanxiong, ganqi (dry lacquer), zhi xiangfu, oufen (lotus root starch, used raw), old white garlic stem (老白韭根).
Right: make into powder; form into mung-bean-sized pills with genuine shenqu paste. Each day take one hundred pills on an empty stomach with boiled water.
translator_notes: '禁方' interpreted as a forbidden/sealed formula but translated literally.
'右大順散' retained per the source spelling; possibly a miswriting of 大順散, translated literally.

Parenthetical notes and medicinal enumerations preserved in parentheses; formula names, medicinals, and dosages (jin, liang, qian, fen, he, pill) rendered in standard TCM English terms without rounding or omission.
The pulse-rate values 'one breath seven beats / one breath six beats' translated without omission.
The original note about the duplicated 右脈 was preserved in parentheses.
No modern disease or pathophysiological explanations were added; literal translation prioritized.
Antithetical/parallel structures were not expanded into plain prose.
